questions.q: What is the most accurate description of chaos engineering as a practice?
options: Randomly disabling production systems to see what happens, without any plan
A purely theoretical exercise done on an architecture diagram, never against a running system
A disciplined, hypothesis-driven practice: define steady state, form a hypothesis, inject a real failure, compare results
A synonym for load testing under high traffic volume
questions.explain: Chaos engineering follows a scientific method: a steady-state hypothesis is defined, a specific failure is injected, and the result is compared against the hypothesis — it is not undirected disruption.

options: A specific, measurable signal defining normal system behavior, such as checkout success rate staying at or above 99.9%
A guess about which team caused the last outage
The budget allocated for infrastructure in a given quarter
A general feeling that the service is probably fine
questions.explain: The steady-state hypothesis must be concrete and measurable so there is something precise to compare against once the failure is injected.

questions.q: What did Netflix's original Chaos Monkey tool actually do?
options: It simulated failures only in a staging environment, never in production
It automatically rolled back every deployment that failed a unit test
It generated synthetic load to stress-test a service's throughput limits
It randomly terminated production EC2 instances to test resilience to real infrastructure failure
questions.explain: Chaos Monkey, part of Netflix's Simian Army, randomly killed production instances so engineers could find out — on their own terms — whether the system tolerated that kind of real failure.

questions.q: Why does a chaos experiment inject a real failure rather than only reasoning about one in an architecture review?
options: Because architecture reviews are not allowed to discuss failure scenarios
Because real injected failure reveals how the system's actual behavior compares to what the team believes, which a whiteboard discussion cannot verify
Because injecting a real failure is cheaper than holding a meeting
Because unit tests already cover every failure scenario a system could face
questions.explain: A whiteboard discussion can only test what the team believes about the system; injecting a real failure tests what the system actually does, which is the whole point of the practice.

questions.q: What does chaos engineering test that load testing does not?
options: How the system behaves when traffic volume increases steadily over time
Whether the user interface renders correctly on mobile devices
How the system behaves when a specific real component or dependency fails, not just when volume is high
Whether the codebase passes static analysis
questions.explain: Load testing exercises the system under volume; chaos engineering exercises it under a specific, realistic failure of a dependency or component — a different and complementary question.
